plotSections.title: Where the last session left off
bullets: In the cave, Walker talked with Vecna, waited until Vecna left, and kept investigating. He learned what a ley-line convergence is, along with other pieces of his situation.
The rest of the party finished with Carlkin, drank at the pub, and went out to explore the next morning.
Last session's openings were not fixed: size and location could vary with motivation, abilities, and durability, and the openings interact with the surroundings and with each other.
Play resumes at midday on the seventh day. There are two short activity windows before Walker's training montage in the power-chamber situation he has found himself in.

plotSections.title: Toward the convergence
bullets: Walker plans to go to the convergence and settles on calling the site an obelisk after trying pyramid and monolith.

Elrus advised the convergence because it lights up the map. The other lead is Elrus's table in Nyx, to see whether it adds information or holds another gold eagle marker. The markers where Elrus was living, in the cave, were generic and not the fancy gold eagle.
Walker flies toward the convergence and picks up Plymouth Gawater, who missed the earlier discoveries. Walker is unsure Plymouth has anything further to add.

plotSections.title: Primal stones and the cosmic loom
bullets: A primal stone is elemental energy poured into a gem and stabilized. Set into a weapon, Walker's fire stone would add fire and magic damage. A worn earring would not do that for a bow; worn, it could only be a focus for his own fire. A loose stone is not enough for anyone else: it has to be set into a conduit such as a wand or weapon, so handing Gerk the stone alone would not let him cast fire.

With a good enough roll and Elrus's help, Walker may be able to make one. Capacity scales with the energy spent and with how pure and unflawed the gem is, and forming the stone costs more energy than it stores. Ley-line convergences make the work much easier, which is why they are sought after.
Walker's primary element is fire, the first he learned. He can also call water, light, and darkness, and he can already spend energy stored in his gemstones.

Raw energy in those gems is safe only for dragonriders, who can draw it in and out through their dragon links. Glimmen, and possibly another dragon, could use it to a lesser extent. For someone like Plymouth it is an unstable charge: tripping it destroys the vessel and throws magical shrapnel. A finished primal stone stabilizes that energy so others can use it through the conduit.

Setting a stone into an object takes a cosmic loom, a magical containment table that also goes by other names. It looks like an altar with an upside-down table: four pillars, one at each corner, generate a field that holds the energy. Elrus has tried this once or twice, does not know where a loom is now, and could start the carvings and look for pillar materials, but that would take time. Walker does not remember seeing one. Plymouth might be able to do the setting.

Elrus, surprised Walker was not told and hearing they have found a convergence, wants his equipment, but there is no time: Walker's training is imminent, and Elrus calls him a fledgling. Elrus was still describing how the gems must be cut, and how a fire stone might support fire-based effects including something defensive, when Walker stepped away.

plotSections.title: Doorway practice and the tavern
bullets: While Walker is away, the others train and expect on the order of a day before he returns. Ciri throws rocks at Gerk while he opens doorways from different directions. Gerk says the day's work is going well and that the Doorman ability seems fine after Sylan pushed him to rein it in.

Training ends and Sylan, Gerk, and the others head for the pub or the keep to find Dana. Gerk says someone there has been adept at sorting out his doorway problems; that person is not named. Sylan hopes Dana has recovered from the visit to Carlkin. She was there for the first part, and Sylan thinks the party sometimes embarrasses her.

They arrive while Dana is quietly playing. She waves and keeps playing. Sylan greets Ciri as if she has just returned; Ciri says she has been with the group the whole time and has not gone anywhere. On royalty she says she does not know, then that she is still royal, and that she is apparently a very good bar owner. Sylan has not been to the bar often but thinks it is doing well, and Ciri tells him not to worry about it.

Dana has been away and is unsure whether she is at the brewery or elsewhere. The table tells her she can be at the bar with Ben, in the forest with the others, or at the convergence. She chooses the bar.

A map mark for bees is a short, successful hive adventure that supplied the tavern's mead. Sylan remembers a crew of about three and guesses Walker, Ord, or a younger Gerk. The DM says it was Sylan, Patty, and at least one other person.

Sylan plans a quiet night, morning prep, and a meeting with Walker the next day, hoping Walker has more information. Gerk has nothing particular planned. Sylan intends to talk with Ord about a lantern and a staff, hoping Ord figures out how to use them.

plotSections.title: The helmet and Nyx Cage's heat stone
bullets: Walker's flight is short. He and Plymouth reach an island where the obelisk stands north of the guild hall. Plymouth asks about a cosmic loom; Walker knows nothing about it. Plymouth describes it as a magical item they cannot make, at least not quickly, and says stones can be created at the convergence but still need the loom to be set into an item. He bases that on Elrus's account of ley lines.

A finished stone can be offensive, defensive, or utility magic, depending on how many stones are used, how valuable they are, and how they are set. Examples include a blade that flames, burns hot, or both, and a ring or blanket that gives warmth. An item made with Walker's stones could give Gerk fire protection or offensive fire.

Walker already has a warmth item, can breathe underwater, and has darkvision. He wants stones in his helmet: light separated from fire for night vision, heat detection, and a way to see through magical darkness. He will not sacrifice the jewelry he worked to make. Plymouth says it is possible with time and a very powerful primal stone, but separating light from fire and also detecting heat is complex. Several stones would be easier: one for light, one for heat, and possibly a third whose illusion magic is reversed to pierce magical darkness, which he describes as an inverse illusion or an absence of light. Walker says that if the helmet cannot do this, the project is not worth doing.

Plymouth says the helmet can wait: Walker's training matters more. The convergence is still worth the trip because it is a rare, highly magical landmark, hard to see again for a very long time, and experiencing it would help that training more than any item made there.
Plymouth has no gems or diamonds. He forgot most of his equipment, bought only odds and ends in Sunder, and is carrying powdered dragon liver.

Walker asks whether a stone that already has a magical property can take more. Plymouth says that in an unbound state it would be highly unstable, would take a great deal of energy to contain, and could damage the caster or the item if the item cannot hold the energy. Walker shows his heat stone and his keystone. Plymouth refuses any experiment on the keystone. The heat stone only keeps its bearer warm, and more fire magic might be poured into it, but when Plymouth examines it he finds that without proper containment any added energy would make it implode immediately. Walker drops the idea.

The warming stones were bought in Agenheim because it was cold, on the way toward Jotunheim and the seeing stones. The seller was Nyx Cage the Ice Mage. He offered a discount if the party went to Helheim and stole a peace treaty between the people of Helheim, described as goliaths, and the giants. The party did not take the job. No one remembered his name until the DM supplied it. Walker allows that Nyx Cage could be an alias; Plymouth finds the name shady and does not know him.

plotSections.title: The shifted obelisk
bullets: The obelisk stands on a small grassy island in rolling field: no base, bare ground, slightly angled and slightly embedded, with grass growing around it. The ground at the corrected ley-line point feels no different from the rest of the field.

Walker's notes and drawings of the shift are gone. He remembers the mountain to the west, the obelisk to the north, and a shift of about twenty degrees off center. They have traveled about 5.6 miles. Facing back toward the guild, the ley line sits to the right of the obelisk, about a hundred yards. Walker treats the twenty-degree figure as far too large.

plotSections.title: Forty-two days and the return
bullets: Walker asks Elrus whether they must meditate for the working to succeed. Elrus says no, but they should meditate anyway. From pocket scraps he casts a simple cantrip with a small pebble, scorched moss, and an insect. Light reaches about sixty feet, with another sixty feet beyond that.

Elrus is not properly equipped and wants everyone to leave and return later. Walker agrees and plans to gather more stones and more energy. They agree to meditate, train, and do more magic training on site before they try again, then return to Midgard.

Walker thinks only about two weeks have passed for him. Elrus checks a watch and says it has been exactly forty-two days, and that Walker has been training the entire time even while being told he still needs to train more.

Walker pins the site for later: from the tower, 0.01 radians to the west, his right when facing the guild, then 5.6 miles. A restatement of two miles northwest at 0.01 radians is corrected to that western heading.

Walker will not imbue primal stones yet. He wants the party's input first. He floats night vision for himself and, less certainly, an instrument that would strengthen Dana's magic, and says the cosmic loom still has to be figured out before he knows how useful a stone would be.

Plymouth takes a collapsible rod from a telescope-like case on his belt. It is about a foot long, with adjustment knobs, and one end is a broad, rounded, three-pronged head. He factors in the convergence and the 5.6-mile distance, plants the rod, and tells everyone to stand close. Electrical energy arcs around it, then a lightning crack and flash carry the group away.

They arrive on a brisk mountaintop overlooking a valley, not on the grassy island and not at the stronghold's front door, which was Plymouth's aim. He recovers the smoldering rod and says he was a little off: a little farther and it would have been quite bad. By his calculations the stronghold is down in the valley. Walker thanks him.

plotSections.title: Morning of the eighth day
bullets: For the group at home it is the morning of the eighth day. They have had no contact from Walker. The morning is brisk, fall is coming in, and thunder and lightning roll in the distance.

Sylan has been up a couple of hours and has been working with Gerk. He checks on Ord. Ord asks for help with his lantern. They plan to work outside in the woods, away from people, for about an hour, as a similar outing worked last time. Sylan expects to ride out again and has an ability ready so they do not blind themselves.

Ord has been trying to regain lost strength and has made no progress. He does not think the loss came from his duel with Gerk. As he remembers it, they were at a place heard as "the orc Tam," his strength went into a little object heard as "a little Ord," and someone else touched it instead of him. He also says he cannot see.

The loss comes from the fight with Gerk's uncle, the Grunkle, which ended with the uncle dying after he had taken some of Ord's strength. Sylan at one point remembered the uncle punching the strength out. A floating Ord appeared and, with Dana involved, solidified into a runic bead or sphere with a rune on it.

Dana could not fix it. Restoration, greater restoration, and everything else she has were already tried. The clue still holds: you cannot restore what is not missing, so the strength is hidden rather than gone. Sylan suggests a monk might explain what the fight did. Ord thinks that is worth pursuing later and wants to deal with the lantern first.

Sylan asks who lives in the keep and guesses about twenty people. The party cannot name them. The roster is on a different map than the one at hand. Mahali is there and earns his place by cooking. Their secrets man, remembered as the rat or the rack guy and chosen for his resourcefulness, is missing; Sylan thought he had taken unscheduled leave, and the DM says the party needs to remember where they left him.

A small white monkey may be a monk or only a special fighter. Ord treats that figure as the little one and asks for the father's name, nearly calling him Benji. The name on the notes is Koji, and Sylan does not remember spending time with him. A little gold person who makes something gold is Ord's roommate; the name came through as Banshee, then Archie, and the table settled on Ponchi.

plotSections.title: The fused lantern-staff and the white dragon's hoard
bullets: Ord found the lantern in Volga. Sylan found a staff at Shades and Trades, thought the two belonged together, and they were later fused. The lantern was identified at Shades and Trades. It is hooded and finely made, with an aura of evocation. It has two settings, and one of them blinded an entire room. A spoken command made something happen; trying to undo it made something else happen, and the effect was hard to dismiss.

The components are a Staff of the Lantern Bearer and a Lantern of Revealing. Sylan also remembered the staff as the Staff of the Lantern Keeper, and the lantern's name was still wrong in memory, including "lantern of the staff keeper." The inscription is not in the current notes. The two items were already drawn together and fused in an earlier impromptu working when the lantern's inscription was read. The DM confirms they are fused and cannot be separated. The result is one staff-and-lantern. Ord has seen a shadowy ethereal vision from it.

On November 3, 2025, Ord experimented with it and saw into the Ethereal Plane. That was set aside because the previous session ended with an emissary arriving with a finger in a box. The last time Ord used it he could see into the Ethereal, blinded himself until Sylan cured him with lesser restoration, and no spirits were present. Asked for the phrase that ignites it, Ord offers "Brightest day in darkness," and later a working oath that no evil shall escape his sight and that those who worship evil should beware his power. The DM treats the wording as still being workshopped.

The pieces come from the white dragon's hoard. The DM's notes date that haul to November 3 of the previous year. Counted wealth is about two dozen gemstones, art objects, mundane goods, 500 platinum, 60,000 gold, 11,000 silver, and 4,100 copper. Sylan remembers four or five magic items. Dana tracked her own magic broom and a set of bone dice and did not write down most of the other magic items.

Dana's other hoard notes: a small shrine with a statuette, a brazier, and an altar to a god of dragon minions; a scroll with a poem; the skull of a fiend or celestial; seven candlesticks marked with a holy symbol; a gold bracelet; a gold locket with a painted portrait; a copper chalice; and two carved bone statuettes. Sylan gave the gold birdcage to the crew. A box of turquoise animal figurines was also in the hoard; Ord inspected them and left them behind, and Sylan suspects they might turn into creatures.

Dana identifies the undead woman tied to the hoard as Lady Meriwether, a name the table connects to Merryweather in Sleeping Beauty. The white dragon's own name is not recovered; Sylan's line that the name is "Lost of Time" reads as the name being lost to time.

A separate hoard item, a ring or bracelet, went to Ciri. It shoots starbursts that turn into fireballs. Guesses at the name include Nightfall and Starfall. Nobody present remembers the actual name, and Ciri is away.

plotSections.title: The phylactery question
bullets: Sylan wants the party, once Walker is back, to test whether the hat or helm Walker has been wearing is the lich's phylactery, and to decide whether to do that in the open or in secret. Dana is already comparing her notes and books to a Legend Lore prophetic vision on that question.

Sylan worries the lich can make another phylactery and shrug the loss off. Dana's plan is to destroy the phylactery and kill the lich before he can form a replacement. Sylan expects that holding the soul would make the lich easier to find, and Dana agrees that is a fair assumption.

Sylan flags two conditions: the item must actually be a phylactery, and Walker must not have been corrupted by wearing it. He remembers the first time Walker put it on as questionable. Walker, just back, brushes it off with "Wouldn't you like to know?"

plotSections.title: Ethereal sight in the woods
bullets: Ord and Sylan go to their usual door-testing spot in a wooded strip, away from the stronghold, to repeat the lantern ritual. Ciri is gone. Sylan looks away and closes his eyes. Ord closes his eyes as well, because the last activation blinded him.

Ord speaks the workshopped oath and calls the staff-lantern's light. The forest flashes. For Ord the effect is also an audible tone. He then sees the Ethereal Plane in grayscale, semi-opaque and ghostly, with shadows moving through the woods that were not visible before. The lantern burns a desaturated blue, and Ord's eyes match it: flat color, no pupils, with a little smoke when he blinks.

Sylan appears several shades darker than the surroundings. About half a dozen cloudy, semi-translucent figures mill around him, half above him and half passing through him. Ord tells him what he sees, wonders whether the sight pierces magical darkness, and slowly brings the staff toward the nearest figure without quite touching it.

That being startles, looks from the lantern to Ord, and grabs the crook of the staff, trying to wrench it away. Its face is gaunt, its eyes crazed, and its body is only half solid, but it can grip the staff. Ord holds on and asks whether it can hear him and who it is. A wail answers inside his head. As it screams, its edges fray and burn away like paper. The other five turn, howl, and move toward the lantern. Soon three or four are pulling, and the first is about half burnt away. Sylan only sees the staff jerk and asks if Ord is all right.

Dana is in her tower. She knows which way they went and, after the flash, watches from afar with her broom ready. Gerk is in a shady spot within thirty feet, watching rather than taking part. He looked at the light and fails a Wisdom save: 3 on the die, plus 5 from Ord's nearby ward, for a total of 8 against a DC that needs to break 10. He is blinded and fumbling on the ground.

plotSections.title: The black beacon and the spirits
bullets: Ord asks Sylan to grab the staff and wrench it back. Sylan does. When Sylan's hand closes on the active staff, the lantern's light becomes incandescent shadow, a roiling ball of shadow glowing inside it. The spirits erupt outward and drop around Ord and Sylan as incomplete physical bodies. From the stronghold the moment reads as a beacon of eternal blackness rising from the treeline: a swirling mass of ink with a shadowy wave that can be felt passing through everything. Dana calls it a giant pillar of darkness. The air crackles, and the glade is both the darkest and the brightest it has been.

Once a spirit comes within about four feet of Sylan while he holds the active staff, a vortex sucks it into him. He feels no change. The pull is a byproduct of touching the staff while it is active. Toasting the spirits during the ethereal sight is what led to them being drawn in. Blind Gerk only hears the sucking. He yells that he cannot see and stays on the ground whirling his hammer overhead to keep things off him, not striking.

Sylan does not recognize the figures. They look much alike except one fitter spirit with a large wound down the center of his face, a killing blow. Four are drawn in. The two still outside shade from blue-ethereal toward black and are no longer light-producing. After being pulled in, the remaining spirits crawl the other way and cannot break the pull. Sylan keeps hold. He has dealt with spirits before, did not expect them to follow, and wants to see it through. He says they followed for a reason and that he did not purge anyone.

Ord suggests saying the incantation backwards to shut it off. That attempt is not carried through. The DM notes this use has not been shut off yet, and asks whether they mean to end it or incite something else. Last time, shutting it off did something else.

plotSections.title: Ledzbika and the last spirit
bullets: Ord keeps one hand on the staff and grapples one of the last two spirits. It is half-formed but solid enough to hold, like a ghost given physical form, and it has been brought from the Ethereal onto the material. A magical pull drags it toward Sylan, and Ord's grip is the only thing holding it back.

Ord uses Divine Sense while holding the staff and the spirit, swirling them as part of the cast. Strong evil registers as a noxious odor. Until the end of his next turn he knows the location of any celestial, fiend, or undead in range, and the type, but not a finer subtype. These are undead: spectral spirits made physical. Ord has used Divine Sense once before, in Volga.

The held spirit is an elderly half-elf. He says they have disturbed his peace, demands release, and gives his name as Ledzbika. The table also hears Bannaby, Burton, Barnaby, and Carnaby, and he later says he already gave his name. Sylan can hear him. He says the party pulled them from life and from his rest, that the one who shed the light burned them, and that Sylan, whom he calls a fiend, is sucking the rest of them in. He is trying to return to his abode, not to go to Sylan. He says the woman next door, Claire Belle, stole from him and his family, that his silver is under the floorboards, and that this is why his children are starving. He says he is stuck and must get back to find her. Asked where his abode is, he does not give a place.

A separate raspy voice also demands to be let go, calls them fiends, says they stole from him, and says he was pulled from his floorboards as the party walked by today. He says a friend is sucking them in and taking them somewhere. He is not named. Sylan asks whether these ghosts are from Morgan. That is not answered.

Sylan says he may be able to talk to them again if Ord lets this one go, and that they should settle this first. Ord releases him. As he dematerializes he reaches toward New Navel. The words that go with the gesture are lost. He snaps away. The last spirit clings to a root while being pulled.

Ord grabs the last spirit: an amorphous upper body of an elderly, sickly, pockmarked woman. Unlike the earlier spirits, she death-grips his hand and begs him not to let go. It is not her time, her son does not know and needs to know, and the darkness is pulling her. She never gives her name or her son's, only repeating that they need to know. While Ord holds her she can grip him. The moment he chooses to release her, her hands dematerialize, pass through him, and she is vacuumed away. The area goes oddly quiet.

Sylan and Ord take these figures for spirits from Old Navel, stirred up as the party passed. Sylan suspects something has gone wrong, jokes that it is like a ghost retirement home, and does not think the woman is giving a usable story.

plotSections.title: Walker and Dana reach the glade
bullets: Walker means to leave Plymouth, then go to Grazog. Plymouth asks to be set down at New Navel and says he will make his own way. Sylan says the party badly needs to talk to him. Plymouth scrambles off Glimmen and heads toward New Navel. One or two gatehouse guards hail Walker.

Dana is at the tower window, deep in her books on the phylactery question, when she hears dragon wings. Glimmen and Araden, a dragon several sizes larger than Glimmen, land near the stronghold. The village, used to Glimmen alone, buzzes at the second dragon.

Walker and Dana see the black beacon go up toward the testing grounds. Dana leaves immediately on her broom, which flies 50 feet, and expects to need a couple of turns to arrive. Walker has taken Glimmen back from Plymouth. He tells Elrus there is a change of plans; they had been going to train rather than go on to Grazog. Elrus takes the forest disturbance as the companions. Walker and Araden take off, and Glimmen overtakes the broom.

In the air, Walker asks what is happening. Dana guesses the others are messing with a magical item. She says she was indisposed for a couple of days and that this is what happens when she and Walker are both gone. Walker's line about being gone forty-nine days is a joke he immediately walks back. Sylan calls the scene a literal dark age.

Dana greets them with "Nice of you to show up." While Sylan and Ord still have their hands on the staff, the black beacon is still erupting from the joined hands. Sylan compares it to Call of Cthulhu and lets go after Ord tells him he can. The beacon stops. Dana and Walker see a faint afterimage for a few blinks, then it is gone, and the clearing dies in light.

No more spirits close in. At about sixty feet, hands and silhouettes still flash in and out of the forest edge, but they do not approach. Ord can still see in an almost wireframe style. He ends the sight on purpose: a long blink extinguishes it, and the forest looks ordinary again.

plotSections.title: Reunion
bullets: Gerk is still blind, screaming, and swinging his hammer. He refuses to stop: he is terrified, cannot see, and says his eyes are all he has. Tremorsense tells him something is approaching. Sylan says it is a friend. Gerk fears a mimic and demands proof.

Walker jokes that Sylan should claim to be Gerk's dad, a joke only Gerk would know. Sylan will not use that and does not think Gerk will remember their call phrases. The phrase they land on is "I don't trust the cat man," which Gerk says is the one note he has written down and which Sylan confirms is the first. Walker also throws out "scoop fruit" and "loincloth."

Flapping becomes audible as Glimmen and Araden arrive. Gerk asks to touch Sylan's face to recognize him, keeps the hammer raised, and reaches out ready to strike. Sylan casts lesser restoration through the touch. Gerk's sight returns, he recognizes Sylan, and he picks him up.

Sylan says the staff test left him with problems in New Navel: he thinks he picked up restless souls and may need a couple of days there as a ghost detective, possibly at Carlkin's house, now that Walker is back. He says he thought a little girl might be alone and kept extra spirits so she would have company. Gerk, who has dealt with voices in his head before, panics at being haunted and drops Sylan.

Dana and Walker arrive as the two dragons land beside the forest. Dana scolds Ord, calling him Lord Bronztail, and tells Sylan not to touch magical items that are not his. Gerk insists Sylan haunted him.

The party is together again on the outskirts of Trigash Forest. Ord opened a third eye with the lantern, the staff work drew the spirits in, and the spirits were mixed: some would not leave, and some seemed to be trying to get back to neighbors. What that means is left for next session, as the DM begins to add something about Araden.

chronologicalEvents: The DM recaps the cave: Walker spoke with Vecna, waited for him to leave, investigated further, and learned what a ley-line convergence is.
The other party members finished with Carlkin, spent a night drinking at the pub, and set out to explore the next morning.
The DM recaps that openings could be made at different sizes and locations depending on motivation, abilities, and durability, and that they interact with the surroundings and each other.
It is midday on the seventh day, with two activity windows left before Walker's training montage.

Walker chooses the convergence obelisk. Elrus recommended it because it lights up the map, and Walker also wants to check Elrus's table in Nyx for more information or another gold eagle. The cave where Elrus was living had only generic markers, not a gold eagle.

Flying toward the convergence with Plymouth aboard, Walker confirms primal stones with Elrus: fire energy imbued into a stone, then set in a sword, yields fire and magic damage. Convergences make that crafting much easier, possibly something Walker could do himself with Elrus's help. Walker establishes fire as his primary element and says he can already call fire, water, light, and darkness, and spend the energy stored in his gemstones. He asks what a primal stone adds if he can already do that, what putting a fire earring on his bow would accomplish, and whether imbuing stones into weapons is worth it.

Elrus explains that dragonriders can safely use that raw stored energy and that it is dangerous for anyone else. Primal stones stabilize it for other users once set in a conduit. Gem quality and the energy spent set a stone's strength, and the number, value, and setting decide whether the result is fire protection, offensive fire, or a utility such as warmth. Gerk could not cast from a loose stone. Setting a stone takes a cosmic loom, which Elrus does not know how to find, though he could try to build one over time. Walker does not remember a cosmic loom. Elrus has no equipment on hand and cannot delay Walker's imminent training to fetch it. He offers to start pillar carvings later, begins a fire-stone example and the gem cuts, and Walker steps away as the scene pauses.
Meanwhile Gerk practices opening doors from different directions while Ciri throws rocks at him. Gerk says the Doorman training seems fine. Sylan asks whether Gerk had the ability the whole time.

Sylan assumes Ciri has returned from a journey. Ciri says she never left, that her royalty situation is complicated, that she is still royal, and that she is a successful bar owner. Sylan says the bar seems to be doing well.
Dana notices a map mark for bees. The group ties it to a one-session hive adventure that supplied the tavern's mead hives, and the DM identifies Sylan and Patty among that short crew.

Dana does not know where her character is and chooses the bar. The others finish training and travel back to meet her at the pub or the keep. Sylan asks whether she has recovered from the visit to Carlkin. They reach the bar while Dana is playing, plan to spend the rest of the day there, prepare in the morning, and see Walker tomorrow. Sylan plans to ask Ord about the lantern and staff Sylan gave him.

Walker and Plymouth land on the island after the short flight, with the obelisk north of the guild hall. Plymouth says the convergence is a rare, highly magical landmark worth the trip because it will help Walker's training. Walker proposes imbuing his helmet for night vision, heat vision, and sight through magical darkness without using his personal jewelry. Plymouth says that is possible but complex, easier with multiple powerful stones, and that a cosmic loom is required. Walker remains undecided about primal stones. Plymouth has no spare gems, only Sunder odds and ends and powdered dragon liver.

Walker asks whether more magic can be added to a stone that is already magical, and shows a heat stone and a keystone. Plymouth forbids adding anything to the keystone. He says the heat stone might accept more fire magic, then examines it and warns that forcing more magic in, especially in a free state and without containment, is unstable and can destroy the caster or the item; the stone would implode. It otherwise works as advertised. Walker abandons the plan.

The party cannot remember which -heim they bought the heat stones in. Plymouth says Agenheim, from Nyx Cage the Ice Mage, who gave Walker the item and wanted them to steal the goliath-giant peace treaty in Helheim for a discount. They never did the job.

At the obelisk, Walker reconstructs the ley-line offset from notes and memory: mountain west, obelisk north, about twenty degrees off center, and the drawings are gone. After about 5.6 miles of travel, Plymouth places the line about a hundred yards to the right of the obelisk when facing the guild. The spot feels like ordinary rolling grass. The obelisk sits angled on bare ground with no base.

Elrus says meditation is not required for the working but should be done anyway, then casts an under-equipped cantrip using a pebble, scorched moss, and an insect. It throws bright light about sixty feet and another sixty feet beyond. He calls off the real attempt until he has proper equipment. Walker agrees to gather more stones and energy. They agree to train further and return to Midgard.

Elrus's watch reads exactly forty-two days. Walker had felt about two weeks and had not registered the training. He pins the site as 0.01 radians west from the tower, then 5.6 miles, and declines to imbue primal stones until he talks with the party, citing night vision, Dana, and the cosmic loom.

Plymouth plants his foot-long adjustable rod after accounting for the convergence and the 5.6 miles, and the group is told to stand close. Energy arcs around the rod. Walker agrees, and lightning carries them from the grassy knoll to a brisk mountaintop above a valley, rather than the stronghold's front door. Plymouth recovers the smoldering rod, stows it, and admits the landing was off: the stronghold is below.

On the morning of the eighth day, the others still have had no in-game word from Walker. The morning is brisk, fall is arriving, and thunder sounds in the distance. After working with Gerk, Sylan checks on Ord. They agree to take Ord's Volga lantern and the staff Sylan found at Shades and Trades into the woods, away from people, and experiment without blinding themselves, possibly fusing the two. Sylan recalls that he already fused the Volga lantern with that staff.

They revisit lost strength. Ord says his own strength still has not returned and that he can't see; he traces the loss to a moment when his strength went into a small object someone else touched, not to the duel with Gerk. The party also goes over Gerk's lost strength: his uncle, the Grunkle, died at the end of that fight after taking some of it, and a floating form solidified into a rune-marked bead. Restoration, including Dana's magic and greater restoration, has failed because the strength is hidden in Gerk rather than missing. Sylan suggests finding a monk who might explain the fight. Ord wants to start with the lantern, and the party turns to the staff.

They try to name who lives in the keep. Mahali is the cook. Their secrets man is away without leave, and the DM presses them to remember where they left him. The roster name in front of them is Koji; Sylan does not remember him among the residents, and they confuse him with Benji and with a little white monkey who may be a monk or a fighter. The DM identifies Koji as the father of that monkey. Ord describes a small gold person who makes something gold; the DM identifies that person as Ord's roommate, and Ord names him Ponchi.

Dana reads her notes from the white dragon's hoard, dated November 3 of the previous year: her broom and bone dice, two carved bone statuettes, a gold bracelet, a gold locket with a painted portrait, a copper chalice, gemstones, 500 platinum, 60,000 gold, 11,000 silver, and 4,100 copper, and a shrine to a god of dragon minions. Sylan recalls giving the hoard's gold birdcage to the crew. The DM adds a box of turquoise animal figurines, which Ord inspected and left behind; Sylan thinks they may become creatures. Sylan guesses an associated name is Lost of Time, and Dana names the undead woman Lady Meriwether.
The table tries to recall Ciri's ring or bracelet, which fires starbursts that become fireballs. Ciri is absent, and the name, Nightfall, Starfall, or something similar, is not recovered.

The DM places the lantern's identification at Shades and Trades and cannot recover the inscription; he sets the real incantation aside to workshop later. His notes put Ord's ethereal experiment on November 3, 2025, immediately after a session in which an emissary arrived with a finger in a box and overshadowed the experiment. Ord describes the hooded lantern as finely made, with an aura of evocation, two settings, one of which blinded a whole room, and a command effect that was difficult to end. He improvises "Brightest day in darkness" as the ignition phrase. Sylan remembers not to look when it goes off. They confirm one item as the Staff of the Lantern Keeper. The paired lantern's name stays unresolved, as does whether the two can still be separated. Ord heads for the woods to recite the inscription, and the DM confirms the two items are fused.

Sylan proposes checking whether Walker's hat is a phylactery, in daylight or in secret, and worries it may have corrupted him. Dana says the phylactery must be destroyed and the lich killed before a new one is made. The party considers that possessing the soul would make him easier to find.

In the woods at the door-testing grounds, away from the others, Ord activates the fused staff and lantern and recites a paladin-style charge. Sylan looks away. Ord closes his eyes, having gone blind the last time. The DM confirms the Lantern of Revealing and the Staff of the Lantern Bearer fused after the inscription was read. The forest flashes. Ord perceives the Ethereal Plane in ghostly grayscale, with shadows moving in the woods. His eyes and the lantern glow a flat, desaturated blue. Sylan shows darker than the surroundings, with about six cloudy figures drifting around and through him.

Ord extends the staff toward the nearest figure. It grabs the crook and tries to pull the lantern free. Its face is gaunt and its form is only half solid. Ord asks who it is. A wail sounds inside his head, the figure's edges burn away, and the other five howl and advance. Sylan grabs the staff and wrenches it back toward Ord. Three or four spirits are on it, the first is about half gone, and the lantern jerks in Ord's hand.
Gerk, within thirty feet and having looked at the light, fails a Wisdom save, given both as a 7 and as 3 + 5 = 8, and is left blind on the ground. Dana watches from her tower. Ciri is gone.

Walker, back from mountainside training with Glimmen and the much larger Araden, plans to drop Plymouth Gawater at New Navel and then go to Grazog. The dragons land by the stronghold. The village reacts, gatehouse guards hail Walker, and Plymouth walks off toward New Navel on his own. Dana researches whether the helmet is the phylactery as they land.

As Sylan's grip lands, the lantern turns to incandescent shadow, the spirits fall as unfinished physical forms, and a beacon of blackness erupts from the treeline. Spirits within about four feet of Sylan are vacuumed into him. The glade crackles. He feels nothing and keeps hold of the staff. He recognizes none of them. One has a killing wound down the center of his face; the rest crawl against the pull and cannot escape.
Dana sees the pillar of darkness and flies her broom from the tower toward it. Gerk, blind on the ground, hears the vacuum, sits screaming, and whirls his hammer.

More spirits are sucked in. Ord starts speaking the incantation backwards to turn the effect off. The DM says this use has never been shut off, and recalls that Ord's earlier use, placed in Volga, showed him the Ethereal Plane and blinded him until lesser restoration. Four spirits are gone and two remain. The remaining spirits look shaded black rather than blue ethereal, and are physical enough to grab.

Ord holds the staff and grapples one remaining spirit, pinning a now-physical elderly half-elf against the pull toward Sylan. The spirit demands to be released, says they have disturbed his peace, and says he is not trying to reach Sylan but must return to his abode. A separate raspy voice also demands freedom and calls them fiends. Ord uses Divine Sense. The spirits register as undead, spectral spirits made physical, type only and with no subtype. Strong evil smells noxious.

The held spirit says the woman next door, Claire Belle, stole his silver from under the floorboards and left his children starving. He says the one who shed light on them burned them, insists he already gave his name, and refuses Sylan. The party also hears the name Ledzbika but does not cleanly catch it. Sylan asks whether the ghosts are from Morgan and gets no answer. The raspy voice says he was pulled from his floorboards as they walked by, and that their friend is sucking the spirits in. Sylan begins to offer that he might be able to do something.

Sylan tells Ord to let the held spirit go so they can settle this before talking to anyone else, and maybe speak to them again. Ord releases him. He dematerializes, reaching toward New Navel, and snaps away. The last spirit, a sickly elderly woman, clings first to a root and then to Ord. She begs him to hold on so she can tell her son something before the darkness takes her, but she gives no name and no clear message. Sylan agrees they are not getting anywhere and says something has gone wrong.

Walker, having set Plymouth off Glimmen, sees Dana, tells Elrus the plan has changed, and they leave the Grazog errand. He flies with Araden, and Glimmen overtakes Dana's broom. From the sky they overtake the dark vortex and match pace with the party. Dana tells Walker she thinks the others are using a magical item and that things went wrong while she and Walker were away.

Ord releases the woman. Her hands dematerialize, she loses physical purchase, and she is vacuumed away. The area goes quiet. While Gerk keeps screaming, the hands joined on the staff pour a black luminescent beacon into the sky. Sylan lets go and the beacon dies, leaving a brief afterimage for Dana and Walker. Spirits no longer approach. Silhouettes and hands still flicker about sixty feet out at the forest edge. Ord still sees the forest as a wireframe, then wills the spirit-sight off; after a long blink his vision is normal.

Sylan tries to stop blind, hammer-swinging Gerk. Gerk's tremorsense picks up someone approaching; he suspects a mimic and will not trust it. They use the written call phrase "I don't trust the cat man," which Sylan confirms. Wingbeats arrive. Gerk holds the hammer ready, reaches to touch Sylan's face, and Sylan casts lesser restoration. Gerk can see and recognizes him.

Sylan explains the staff test and says he may have gathered restless souls, including company for the little girl, and may have to do ghost-detective work in New Navel at Carlkin's. Gerk panics about being haunted. Dana and Walker land on the two dragons, and Dana scolds Ord and Sylan. Asked whether the hat has corrupted him, Walker does not answer directly and says, "Wouldn't you like to know?"
The session ends on the outskirts of Trigash Forest, with the beacon and the spirits unresolved.

Walker.existing: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter, Gatekeeper of The Reach, bonded to Glimmen.
notes: Last session he spoke with Vecna in the cave, waited until Vecna left, and learned what a ley-line convergence is.
He flies to the convergence obelisk on Elrus's advice, with Plymouth Gawater aboard, and also wants Elrus's table in Nyx checked for another gold eagle or more information.

Fire is the element he learned first and treats as primary. He can also call water, light, and darkness, and he can spend energy already stored in gemstones. Dragon-linked people can move that stored energy safely. He had not told Elrus he had found a convergence.

He does not remember a cosmic loom. He is considering primal stones and wants them set in his helmet for night vision, heat detection, and sight through magical darkness. He already has darkvision, can breathe underwater, and carries a heat stone. He will not use the personal jewelry he worked hard to make, and he drops the project unless the helmet can see what he wants.

He carries a heat stone bought in Agenheim from Nyx Cage and a keystone. He jokes about modifying the keystone, then accepts Plymouth's refusal. After the implosion warning he will not feed the heat stone more magic.

At the obelisk he reconstructs a lost note: mountain to the west, obelisk to the north, about twenty degrees off the ley line. Facing the guild, the true line is about a hundred yards to the right. He restates that offset as about half a degree, or 0.01 radians.
He agrees to leave, gather more stones and energy, and return. His return pin, after he corrects an earlier 'two miles northwest,' is from the tower, 0.01 radians west, then 5.6 miles.

Elrus's watch says Walker has been training for exactly 42 days. Walker experienced about two weeks. He will not imbue a primal stone yet; he wants the party's advice. His own idea is night vision. He also suggests a bard instrument for Dana and says the cosmic loom still has to be sorted out before he knows whether a stone helps.

He has not contacted the stronghold group during this absence. He and Plymouth arrive by lightning teleport on the mountain above the stronghold, marked there by thunder on the morning of the eighth day. He returns from the training full of energy, with Glimmen and Araden.

He means to drop Plymouth Gawater at New Navel and then go to Grazog. One or two gatehouse guards hail him. When the black beacon rises he tells Elrus the plan has changed, leaves the Grazog trip, and flies after Dana. Glimmen overtakes her broom.
On arrival he asks what is going on. A claim of being gone forty-nine days is a joke he immediately walks back. He sees the beacon vanish when the staff is released.

He is back with the party as the two dragons land beside the forest. He supplies the recognition lines 'I don't trust the cat man,' 'scoop fruit,' and 'loincloth,' and jokes that Sylan should claim to be Gerk's dad.

The hat he has been wearing is the party's candidate for the lich's phylactery. Sylan remembers the first time Walker put it on as questionable. Asked if it has corrupted him, Walker does not answer directly.
personality: Fixated on a helmet that lets him see anything he wants, including through magical darkness, and impatient with limits on that idea.
quotesThemes: He keeps pressing Elrus for why a primal stone is worth the energy if he can already call the elements himself.
I want to be the darkness.
I just want to be able to see anything I want to see.
Mathematics is critical to flying.
Wouldn't you like to know?

Vecna.existing: Elder god of liches who watches from the periphery and pursues hidden knowledge.
notes: Spoke with Walker in the cave last session, then left. Walker investigated further after he was gone.

Elrus.existing: Walker's hidden ally in the coming confrontation.
notes: He is the dragonrider instructing Walker. He advised the convergence because it lights up the map. His table in Nyx is a lead for more information or another gold eagle; the markers in the cave where he was living were generic.

He can help Walker make primal stones, and with a good enough roll Walker may be able to do it himself. He is surprised he was not told a convergence had been found. He has tried once or twice to set such stones into objects and thinks Plymouth may be versatile enough to do that setting.

He has none of his equipment with him and wants to circle back for it. He is told there is no time, calls Walker a fledgling, and says training is imminent. He does not know where a cosmic loom is. He could start the carvings and try to procure pillar materials, which would take time.

At the obelisk he says the working does not require meditation, but that Walker should meditate regardless. From a pebble, scorched moss, and an insect he casts a simple cantrip whose light reaches about 60 feet and then another 60 feet. He lacks the right equipment, postpones the real working, and wants meditation, training, and more magic practice at the site before a later return to Midgard.

His watch reads exactly 42 days. He says Walker has been training that whole time and still needs to train more. He offers to imbue primal stones on the spot. Walker declines until he talks with the party.

He is with Walker when they land at the stronghold. He had framed the next step as training instead of Grazog. When the forest beacon appears, Walker tells him the plan has changed. Elrus treats the disturbance as the companions, and he and Walker fly after Dana.
personality: Pushes training and meditation even when the immediate working does not require them, and will not attempt the ley-line working without proper equipment.
quotesThemes: No, but you should meditate regardless.
You need to train more. You've trained the entire time.

Plymouth Gawater.existing: Gnome artificer and party ally who explains the Great Eldarin Tree, keystones, and Mother's Prayer.
notes: Walker picks him up on the flight to the convergence. He missed the earlier discoveries. He explains primal stones from Elrus's account of ley lines and says a cosmic loom is required to set them into an item. He cannot readily make a loom, and it would take time. He does not know Walker to have any prior knowledge of one.

He treats the convergence as a rare, highly magical landmark that will advance Walker's training more than the helmet project, and one Walker will not readily see again for a very long time. He calls the local condition an unstable free state, where forcing more magic into an existing item is dangerous.

He has no gems or diamonds. He forgot most of his equipment, bought odds and ends in Sunder, and is carrying powdered dragon liver. Elrus thinks he might be able to set primal stones into objects. Raw energy stored in Walker's gems is unsafe for him: drawing it out would take heavy magical protection, and tripping it would destroy the item and throw magical shrapnel.

He refuses to add magic to the keystone. He says a heat stone might take more fire magic, then rules that extra energy without proper containment would make Walker's stone implode immediately. He names the seller as Nyx Cage the Ice Mage in Agenheim and finds that name shady. He places the true ley line about a hundred yards to the right of the obelisk when facing the guild.

He carries a foot-long collapsible rod in a telescope-style case on his belt, with turnable sections and a broad rounded three-pronged head. Set for the convergence and the 5.6-mile distance, planted, it arcs with electrical energy and lightning-transports the group. He aimed for the stronghold's front door and landed on the mountain above it. He says a little farther off would have been quite bad, judges the stronghold to be in the valley below, then cleans the smoldering rod and returns it to his belt.
He rides in on Glimmen, asks to be dropped at New Navel, and walks off that way at a brisk pace before the party can talk to him. Sylan says the party needs to talk to him badly.
personality: Treats overloading magical items as dangerous and refuses to attempt it on a keystone or this heat stone.
quotesThemes: Without proper containment, putting more magical energy into the heat stone would make it implode immediately.
A little further and it would have been quite bad, but all's well that starts well.

notes: A dragon linked this way can use the energy stored in Walker's gems, to a lesser extent than a dragonrider.
Carries Walker and Plymouth to the stronghold. The village is used to Glimmen. Plymouth dismounts and leaves for New Navel.

Then carries Walker, with Araden alongside, toward the forest beacon and overtakes Dana's broom. Wingbeats are audible as the two dragons arrive while Sylan is proving himself to blind Gerk. They match pace with the party over the dark vortex and land beside the forest.

Araden.existing: A magically capable companion brought secretly to The Reach.
notes: A dragon several sizes larger than Glimmen. Arrives with Glimmen near Langdale Stronghold. The village, used to Glimmen alone, buzzes at the second dragon.
Cited as agreeing to leave the Grazog trip and go toward the forest disturbance. Flies with Walker and Glimmen after Dana and matches pace over the beacon.

Gerk.existing: Half-orc barbarian, Doorman and Child of the Great Eldarin Tree.
notes: Practices doorways by opening them from different directions while Ciri throws rocks at him. He says the day of training is going well and the Doorman ability seems fine. Sylan had pushed him to rein the ability in. He says someone has been adept at helping with his doorway problems, and that the recent help has been useful. He does not answer whether he has had the ability the entire time.

Returns to the tavern with the others and has nothing special planned there. He treats his heat stone as a hot rock he puts in his pants. A loose primal stone would not let him create fire; it has to be set into an object that releases the energy.

The strength Ord lost to the Grunkle is hidden inside Gerk. Restoration and greater restoration cannot return it. The clue is that you cannot restore what is not missing. Sylan first remembered the uncle punching the strength out of Gerk.

Stays at the door-testing spot in the shade and watches the lantern trial. Within 30 feet he looks toward the light and fails a Wisdom save: 3 plus about +5 from Ord's nearby ward, total 8, against a DC that must break 10. He is blinded, on the ground, and can hear the spirits being sucked in. He considers opening a door to light.

He remains blind through the beacon and the aftermath, screaming and whirling his hammer overhead to keep things away. He is not moving to attack. He says he is terrified and that his eyes are all he has. He will not stop.

Tremorsense lets him feel someone approaching. He suspects a mimic and demands proof. The one note he has written down is 'I don't trust the cat man.' He holds the hammer ready in one hand and reaches with the other to touch Sylan's face.

Lesser restoration restores his sight. He recognizes Sylan, hugs him, and lifts him up, then asks what they did to his eyes. He has had voices in his head before and is furious at the idea Sylan haunted him. He says he cannot afford to be haunted. He tells Sylan to do the New Navel ghost work at Carlkin's house.
personality: While blinded he is panicked and mistrustful, defaults to the hammer, and refuses to trust a voice he cannot verify.
quotesThemes: I am terrified. I can't see. My eyes are all I have.
You could be like a mimic.
I can't believe you haunted me.
openQuestions: Did Gerk have the doorway ability the entire time?

notes: Throws rocks at Gerk during doorway practice.

At the tavern she says she has been with the group the whole time and has not traveled away. She says she does not know whether the royalty matter is sorted, and also that she is still royal. She calls herself a hell of a bar owner. Sylan thinks the bar is doing well despite his rare visits.
She is believed to be carrying a ring or bracelet from the white dragon hoard that shoots starbursts which turn into fireballs. Nightfall and Starfall were both suggested. The name is not confirmed.
She is absent from the lantern trial and the forest scene. The table establishes she is completely gone from those beats.
quotesThemes: I've been here this entire time.
Don't worry, I'm still royal.
And apparently a hell of a bar owner.
openQuestions: Has Ciri's royalty situation actually been sorted out?

notes: He checks Gerk's doorway practice, says he pushed Gerk to rein the Doorman ability in, and expects about a day before Walker returns. After training he leads the group back toward the pub or the keep to find Dana and hopes she has recovered from Carlkin.

He was on the short hive adventure with Patty that supplied the tavern's mead. He plans a tavern night, morning preparation, and a meeting with Walker tomorrow. He intends to talk to Ord about a lantern and a staff, hoping Ord learns to use them.

On the morning of the eighth day he has already been up a couple of hours and has been working with Gerk before he checks on Ord. He agrees to help with the lantern. They have about an hour. He intends to ride out to the woods again, which worked last time, and says he has an ability prepared so they do not blind themselves.

He found a staff at Shades and Trades and thought it belonged with the lantern Ord found in Volga. The DM later confirms the two are fused. Sylan does not have the fused lantern on his sheet. He remembers the staff as the Staff of the Lantern Keeper and, in play, calls the active item the staff of the lantern bearer. He wants the lantern inscription tried on its own if the pieces can be separated. He remembers the blinding setting and looks away, eyes closed, for this activation.

He recalls the heat-stone landing, then the trip on to Jotunheim and the seeing stones. He suggests a monk might explain what the Grunkle's fight did to Ord's strength. He gave the gold birdcage from the white dragon hoard to the crew. He suspects the turquoise animal figurines might turn into creatures.

He presses the party to test Walker's hat as a phylactery once Walker is back, publicly or in secret. He argues for destroying a phylactery carefully, in case the lich can replace it, and thinks holding the soul would make the lich easier to locate, provided the hat is a phylactery and has not corrupted Walker. He remembers the first time Walker put it on as questionable.

In the ethereal view he is several shades darker than the woods, with about half a dozen cloudy figures milling half above and half through him. He cannot see the spirits; he only sees the staff jerk. He grabs it to wrench it back to Ord and asks whether the sight transfers. He says they should never touch the thing again because it always brings those terrible things, then keeps hold anyway.

Spirits within about four feet are vacuumed into him. He feels no internal change, does not recognize them, and refuses to let go. He says he has dealt with spirits before, did not expect these to follow him, and did not purge anyone. He believes they followed for a reason. The held spirit calls him a fiend who pulls them from rest. He asks whether these ghosts are from Morgan.

He tells Ord to release the first spirit, then pushes to question the last one and compare her story. He thinks these are spirits from Old Navel that the party stirred up while passing, and that something has gone wrong with this one. He agrees to let the woman go. His and Ord's joined hands on the staff throw the black beacon. He lets go after Ord says he can, and the beacon ends.

He approaches blind Gerk, tells him to stop swinging, and offers the call phrases. He confirms 'I don't trust the cat man' is the first. He will not use Walker's joke that Sylan is Gerk's dad. He casts lesser restoration by touch while Gerk feels his face. He previously cured Ord's staff-caused blindness the same way.

He believes the staff test left him carrying restless souls. He may spend a couple of days as a ghost detective in New Navel. Gerk tells him to do that work at Carlkin's house. He says he thought the little girl might be alone, so he kept extra spirits as company for her, and he is not sure he is actually full of ghosts. Dana tells him never to touch a magical item that is not his. He allows that he might be a bad guy for it. Walker's return is what lets him go deal with the New Navel spirits.
personality: Sees the spirit-vacuum through rather than dropping the staff, and treats the spirits' attachment as earned, until Gerk panics and he admits he does not really know what he is carrying.
quotesThemes: We should never touch this thing ever again. It always brings those terrible things.
They were following me. It must have been for a good reason. It doesn't seem like they want to go back.
They've earned it. I didn't purge anybody.
He may have to spend a couple of days as a ghost detective in New Navel because he picked up restless souls.
openQuestions: Whether Sylan is actually carrying ghosts or restless souls.

Dana.existing: Half-elf cleric and Gatekeeper of the Pitel keystone.
notes: She has been away from this stretch and chooses to be at the bar. She learns that the map mark for bees is the hive source for the tavern's mead. She was present for the first part of the visit to Carlkin. Sylan hopes she has recovered from it. When the others return she is quietly playing, waves, and keeps playing.
Her restoration spells, including greater restoration, have not recovered the strength taken in the Grunkle fight. She is the one who had the clue that you cannot restore what is not missing.

From the white dragon hoard she received a magic broom and a set of bone dice. Her old notes still hold that inventory, including the coin counts and the shrine to a god of dragon minions. She had catalogued the coins, gems, art, and mundane goods, and not the other magic items. She identifies the undead woman from that hoard as Lady Meriwether.
She states that destroying a lich requires destroying the phylactery and then killing the lich before he can make a new one. She agrees that holding the soul should make him easier to find.

On the morning of the eighth day she stays in her tower, knows which way Ord and Sylan went, and watches with her broom ready. She is comparing notes and books to a Legend Lore prophetic vision to test whether the helmet could be the phylactery.

She sees Glimmen and Araden arrive, then a pillar of darkness from the woods. She leaves immediately. The broom's flight is 50 feet. She expects to need a couple of turns and is then overtaken by Glimmen.

Once Walker and Araden catch up, she says she does not know what is happening and guesses the others are messing with a magical item. She was indisposed for a couple of days and says this is what happens when she and Walker are both gone.

She and Walker see the black beacon vanish when the staff is released, with the outline lingering for a few blinks. She arrives with Walker as the two dragons land beside the forest. She scolds Ord as Lord Bronztail, asks why Gerk says he was haunted, tells Sylan never to touch a magical item that is not his, and stomps through the group smacking people with her broom.
personality: She takes a full parental tone with the group once she sees the aftermath.
quotesThemes: You can't restore what's not missing.
Nice of you to show up.
This is what happens when we're both gone.
Lord Bronztail, what in the seven arches did you think you were doing?
Sylan, you should never touch any magical item that isn't yours.
openQuestions: Has Dana recovered from the visit to Carlkin?

Ord.existing: Dragonborn paladin and Gatekeeper of Feldspar.
notes: He still has not worked out the lantern and staff Sylan gave him. The lantern was found in Volga and is now fused with the staff Sylan found at Shades and Trades. He wants to test it in the woods, away from people, and he suggested the fusion. Ponchi is his roommate.

He has not regained his lost strength. He does not think the loss came from his duel with Gerk. The clearer account is the fight with Gerk's uncle: the strength was taken, a floating Ord appeared, and it solidified into a runic bead or rune-marked sphere, with Dana involved as it solidified. An earlier memory garbled the place as 'the orc Tam' and the object as 'a little Ord.' Dana's restoration and greater restoration did not work, because the strength is hidden in Gerk. He agrees that finding a monk who understands that fight is a good idea, after the lantern. Sylan remembers that Ord liked boats in a past life and offered Langdale, including a house or a boat, as a place to live.
He currently fights with a shield. Sylan pictures him using the sword and lantern together. He inspected the turquoise animal figurines from the white dragon hoard and left them behind.

The lantern is hooded and finely made. Detect Magic showed an aura of evocation. It has two settings; one blinded the whole room. A command word triggered an effect, undoing it triggered another, and the effect was hard to remove. On November 3, campaign year 25, he saw into the Ethereal Plane and blinded himself until Sylan used lesser restoration. He does not remember the inscription and offers 'Brightest day in darkness' as an ignition phrase. He also speaks an oath that no evil shall escape his sight.

This time he closes his eyes. Activation registers as an audible tone plus a flash, and he does not go blind. While the lantern is lit, the world is grayscale, semi-opaque, and ghostly, and he can see shadows in the woods that were hidden before. His eyes lose their pupils, glow the same desaturated blue as the lantern, and trail a little smoke when he blinks.

He tells Sylan about the figures, extends the staff toward the nearest one, and holds on when it grabs the crook. He asks if it can hear him and who it is. A wail answers inside his head. His nearby ward grants about +5 to a save from within 30 feet; Gerk uses it and still fails. He asks Sylan to grab the staff so he can get control back. He also keeps a hand on the staff and grapples one spirit, holding him against the pull.

He tries to end the effect by speaking the incantation backwards. He recalls that the last attempt to turn it off caused something else to happen. That backward attempt is not carried through. Toasting these spirits during the earlier ethereal sight is what set up the current vacuum.

He identifies the grabbed spirit, aloud, as an elderly half-elf. Divine Sense, which he has used once before, in Volga, reads the spirits as undead with no subtype. Strong evil smells noxious. The spirit accuses the one who shed the light of burning them, which points at Ord's earlier use. He questions the spirit about who he is, where his abode is, and who stole from him, then lets him go when Sylan says to.

He grabs the last spirit, a sickly elderly woman, and tries to learn her name and her son's so he can pass a message. She cannot answer. He says they are not getting anywhere and lets her go. While he is interacting with her she can death-grip his hand; when he consciously releases her, she dematerializes and is vacuumed away. He and Sylan think the spirits are from Old Navel.

He and Sylan had their hands together on the staff when the black beacon went up. After he lets Sylan release it, Ord still has a wireframe-style sight: movement and silhouettes out to about sixty feet, and no further spirits approach. He ends that sight by intending it. A long blink restores normal vision.
Dana addresses him as Lord Bronztail and demands to know what he was doing. He says they were practicing and did not know what would happen.
personality: Down about the strength he cannot get back, and willing to talk about it with Sylan.
quotesThemes: I've been trying, my friend. To no avail.
Brightest day in darkness.
No evil shall escape my sight. But those who worship evil, smite — beware of my power.
openQuestions: Can a monk explain how Ord's strength was hidden in the fight with Gerk's uncle, and how to reach it?

Carlkin.existing: A turtle-like person believed to be back in Langdale.
notes: The party recently visited him. Dana was there for the first part. Sylan hopes she has recovered from it. Gerk tells Sylan to do the New Navel ghost work at Carlkin's house.
Named by the DM as a member of the short crew, with Sylan, on the hive adventure that supplied the tavern's mead. The rest of that crew is not named.
Ice mage in Agenheim who sold the party their heat stones because it was cold. He gave Walker the hot rock they later examine.
He offered a discount if they went to Helheim and stole a peace treaty between the people of Helheim, described as goliaths, and the giants. The party did not do it.
No one had kept his name until it was supplied. Walker says it could be an alias. Plymouth finds the name shady and does not know him.
personality: Willing to trade heat stones for theft of Helheim's peace settlement with the giants.
openQuestions: Is Nyx Cage his real name, or an alias?

notes: Called the Grunkle. His battle with the party ended in his death.

During that fight he took some of Ord's strength. A floating Ord appeared and solidified into a runic bead or rune-marked sphere, with Dana involved in that moment. Sylan first remembered it as the uncle punching the strength out of Gerk. The strength is hidden in Gerk.

Mikkel.existing: Spymaster crew member often left behind when the party departs.
notes: Discussed as the keep's secrets man. The party also calls him the rat and the rack guy, and they chose him for his resourcefulness.
Sylan believes he is missing and took a vacation without asking. The correction is that the party has to remember where they left him.
openQuestions: Where did the party leave their spymaster?

Koji.existing: A stronghold guard who will relocate to the tavern during the evacuation.
notes: His name is the one written on the keep's people map. The DM gives it as the father of the little white monkey while the party tries to identify that figure.
Ord keeps confusing him with Benji. Sylan does not remember him well and has not spent much time with him.
Small figure at the keep, called the little one. Sylan could not remember whether he is a monk or a special fighter. The DM names his father as Koji.
openQuestions: Is the white monkey a monk or a special fighter?

Ponchi.existing: Stronghold guard who was going to relocate to the tavern.
notes: Ord's roommate. Remembered as a little gold person who makes something involving gold. The name was misheard as Banshee and Archie before the table landed on Ponchi.
Undead woman associated with the white dragon hoard. Dana names her Lady Meriwether while reading the hoard notes. The table traces the name to Merryweather.

His hoard, dated in the DM's notes to November 3 of the previous year, is the source of Dana's broom, the bone dice, Ciri's starburst item, the shrine to a god of dragon minions, and the rest of the inventory Dana reads. The fused lantern-staff is also listed among that hoard's magic items.
The party does not recover his name.

Lich.existing: An unidentified lich whose phylactery may be hidden among his chess pieces.
notes: Walker's hat, also discussed as his helmet, is now the item the party wants to test as this lich's phylactery.
The party treats him as able to create a replacement phylactery if the current one is destroyed and he is not killed quickly afterward.
Sylan believes holding the soul from the phylactery would make the lich easier to locate. Dana agrees.
Unnamed god. The white dragon hoard included a small shrine with a statuette, a brazier, and an altar dedicated to a god of dragon minions.

Elderly half-elf spirit among those drawn to the active staff. Ord grabs him as one of the last two, after four others were already sucked in. He is half-formed but physically grabbable, pulled toward Sylan, and Ord's grip is what keeps him back.

Divine Sense reads him as undead, a spectral spirit made physical, with no subtype. He demands release, says his peace was disturbed, and says he is trying to return to his abode rather than go to Sylan. He says the party pulled them from life and from rest, and that the one who shed light on them burned them.
He gives his name as Ledzbika and says he already gave it. Later repetitions are also heard as Bannaby, Burton, Barnaby, and Carnaby.

He names Claire Belle as the woman next door who stole from him and his family. His silver is under the floorboards. He blames her for his children starving and says he is stuck and must get back to find her. He does not say where the abode is.
When released he dematerializes, reaches toward New Navel, and snaps away. A separate raspy voice may be his or another spirit's.
personality: Demands immediate release, calls the party fiends, and treats the questioning as a failure to listen.
quotesThemes: Release me right now, you've disturbed my peace. I am Ledzbika.
I'm not going to that fiend. I'm trying to return back to my abode.
The bitch next door stole my silver, and I must go back and find her, but I am stuck here.
Don't let her fool you. She is a conniving liar who has stolen from us and my family.
openQuestions: Where is his abode, and was the reach toward New Navel the answer?
Whether the raspy voice demanding release is Ledzbika or the other remaining spirit.

notes: Named by Ledzbika as the woman next door. He calls her a conniving liar who stole from him and his family, including silver kept under the floorboards, and blames her for his children starving.
quotesThemes: Don't let her fool you. She is a conniving liar.
openQuestions: Whether Claire Belle is the thief Ledzbika describes.

notes: The last spirit Ord grabs, after Ledzbika is released. An amorphous upper body: an elderly woman with a pockmarked, sickly face. Sylan and Ord take her for a spirit from Old Navel.

She clings to a root while being pulled, then death-grips Ord's hand. She begs not to be let go. She says it is not her time, her son does not know and needs to be told, and the darkness is coming and pulling her. She repeats 'my name' and 'they need to know' but never states a name, the son's identity, or the message.
When Ord consciously releases her, her hands pass through him and she is vacuumed away.
personality: Terrified of being taken, and fixed on getting a message to her son before she goes.
quotesThemes: Don't let me go. It's not my time. My son doesn't know.
The darkness comes. He is pulling me to him.
Tell my son. He needs to know.
openQuestions: What is her name, who is her son, and what must he be told?
Who is the 'he' she says is pulling her into the darkness?

Daisy.existing: A mysterious small girl linked to Gerk.
notes: Sylan says he thought the little girl might be alone, so he kept extra restless souls to keep her company.
About six cloudy, semi-translucent figures were already milling around Sylan in the woods, half above him and half passing through him, unseen until the lantern showed the Ethereal Plane.

The nearest has a gaunt face and crazed eyes, is only half solidified, startles at the lantern, and can grab the staff's crook. It answers Ord with a wail inside the head. Its edges then fray away like burnt paper. The other five howl and move toward the lantern. Three or four pull on it, and the first is about half gone.

When Sylan grabs the staff they erupt outward into incomplete physical bodies. Within about four feet they are vacuumed into him. He does not recognize them and feels no change. They had been ethereal and become more material and black-shaded as the staff acts. Absorbed spirits read as light-producing; the ones still outside are shaded black and are not.

They look much alike except one fitter spirit with a large wound down the center of his face, read as a killing blow. The ones not yet taken crawl against the pull and cannot break it. Four are taken. Two remain: Ledzbika, and then the sickly elderly woman. A raspy, unnamed voice says people stole from him, that he was pulled from his floorboards when the party walked by, and that their friend is sucking them in.

Divine Sense reads them as undead, spectral spirits made physical, with no subtype. Sylan and Ord think they are from Old Navel and were stirred up when the party passed. Sylan also asks whether they are from Morgan. That is not answered.
After the beacon dies, no more spirits close in. At about sixty feet, hands and silhouettes still flash at the forest edge and do not approach.
personality: Startled by the lantern, then aggressive about seizing it. The last woman clings and pleads; the earlier spirits demand release.
openQuestions: Who are these spirits, especially the one with the wound down his face, and is the raspy voice a separate person?
Are they from Old Navel, from Morgan, or from somewhere else?

Nyx.existing: Nyx may hold hobgoblins who know where the lich is hiding.
notes: Elrus has a table in Nyx. The plan is to check it on return for more information or another gold eagle marker.

Convergence.existing: An unnamed flat island of rolling green plains, labeled the grassy atoll on some maps.
notes: The rare, highly magical ley-line landmark Walker and Plymouth fly to. Walker settles on calling the marker an obelisk after also trying pyramid and monolith. An obelisk stands north of the dragon-rider guild hall, on a small grassy island in rolling fields.

The obelisk has no base. It is slightly angled and slightly embedded in bare ground, with grass growing around it. A mountain was to the west and the obelisk itself to the north. The party's chosen working spot feels like ordinary field.

The obelisk is shifted off the true ley line. Walker's old figure was about twenty degrees, which he later treats as far too large. Facing the guild, the true point is about a hundred yards to the right. He pins the return from the tower as 0.01 radians west, then 5.6 miles, after correcting an earlier 'two miles northwest.'
Elrus postpones the actual working until he has proper equipment and recommends meditation and further magic training there. The group then leaves for Midgard.

Dragon Rider Training Grounds.existing: Dragon Rider guild training grounds near the Lost Isles.
notes: The convergence obelisk is north of the guild hall. Facing back toward the guild, the true ley line is about a hundred yards to the right of the obelisk. Walker's notes put a mountain to the west.
Where the party landed and bought heat stones from Nyx Cage the Ice Mage, because it was cold, before continuing toward Jotunheim. Remembered as one of the -heim stops on that journey.
Destination of the untaken job for Nyx Cage: steal a peace treaty between the people of Helheim, described as goliaths, and the giants. The party did not go.

Jotunheim.existing: Homeland of the Juten, associated with Sylan's meditation that revealed Gerk as a destined keeper.
notes: Sylan remembers the party traveling up to Jotunheim after the Agenheim landing because that is where the seeing stones were.

Sitting Stones.existing: A place Sylan has passed through, tied to the Navi and another person's role.
notes: Sylan recalls the seeing stones, under this name, as the reason they drove up to Jotunheim after landing in a -heim.

Midgar.existing: Midgar realm and Arch of Atlas
notes: The group agrees to go back to Midgard rather than finish the ley-line working now. Departure is by Plymouth's planted rod. Electrical energy arcs around it, and everyone is told to stand close. They land on the mountain above Langdale Stronghold.
Where Sylan found the staff later fused to Ord's lantern. The DM believes the lantern was identified here. Sylan wonders aloud whether the place's records have been updated.

Volga.existing: A recent stop whose frozen gatehouse is too faint a memory for Gerk's doorway.
notes: Where Ord found his lantern. He has also used Divine Sense here once before. An earlier use of the lantern, placed by the table in Volga, showed him the Ethereal Plane and blinded him until lesser restoration.

Langdale Stronghold.existing: Party's central stronghold and home base.
notes: Plymouth aimed the return rod at its front door and landed on the mountain above it. He believes the stronghold is in the valley below. There is a large lake below the keep.
