On the morning of the eighth day the weather is surprisingly brisk and fall seems to be coming in. Thunder and lightning sound in the distance as Walker's group arrives. The people at the keep have had no in-game contact from Walker.
Sylan believes about twenty people currently live in the keep. One of the party's maps marks those people; another does not.

Southern stream clearing.existing: A streamside clearing south of Langdale Stronghold, chosen for Gerk's doorway practice.
notes: Called their normal spot, secret spot, and door-testing grounds. Ord and Sylan use it again so the lantern flash stays away from the keep. Gerk watches from shade there. Dana only observes from the stronghold tower.
The black beacon rises from that treeline when Sylan grabs the staff. The DM places the end of this scene on the outskirts of Trigash Forest.
Walker's intended next stop after dropping Plymouth Gawater at New Navel. He abandons that trip when the forest beacon appears. Nothing further is said about Grazog.

New Navel.existing: A familiar stop that sends trade caravans to the party's tavern in Langdale and holds Carlkin's lighthouse.
notes: Plymouth asks to be dropped here and walks toward it on his own.

Ledzbika reaches toward New Navel as he dematerializes. Sylan thinks he has to spend a couple of days here as a ghost detective because of restless souls he picked up. Gerk tells him to do that at Carlkin's house.
Ord asks if these are all the spirits from Old Navel, and Sylan agrees. Sylan thinks they were stirred up when the party walked by.

The session ends on the outskirts of Trigash Forest, which the DM names for clarity. The black beacon, Ord's wireframe sight, and the lurking spirits are all placed here. Silhouettes stayed about sixty feet out and did not close in. What the spirits want is left unresolved.

Elemental energy poured into a gem and stabilized so someone other than a dragonrider can use it. Set in a weapon, Walker's fire stone would deal fire and magic damage. A worn earring would not enchant a separate weapon; it could only focus his own fire.

Strength scales with the energy used to make the stone and with how pure and unflawed the gem is. Making one costs more energy than the stone stores. A ley-line convergence makes the work much easier. Walker may be able to make one himself with Elrus's help if he rolls well enough.
It must be set into a conduit such as a wand or weapon, using a cosmic loom, before someone else can release it. A loose stone would not let Gerk create fire.

Effects depend on how many stones there are, how valuable they are, and how they are set. Options include fire protection, a flaming blade, a red-hot blade, both at once, or utility warmth from a ring or blanket. An item made from Walker's stones could grant Gerk fire protection or offensive fire. Elrus begins a defensive fire example, and that example is cut off.

Walker's helmet idea would take a very powerful stone or, more easily, several: one for light drawn out of fire, one for heat detection, and possibly a reversed illusion stone to pierce magical darkness. He can gather stones and energy, and he declines to imbue any until the party chooses what they should do.
A magical containment table, also described as an altar with an upside-down table. Four pillars at the corners create a field that contains energy. It is used to set a primal stone into an object.

Elrus has tried that setting once or twice and does not know where a loom is now. He could start the carvings and try to procure pillar materials. It would take time. Plymouth says the party cannot readily make one. Walker had never heard of it and does not yet see how an imbued stone would help with the loom in play.
Creating stones at the convergence is a separate step from setting them. The loom is the missing step for Walker's helmet.
Also called a warming stone, a fire stone, and a hot rock. It keeps the bearer warm and is not a primal stone.

The party bought them in Agenheim from Nyx Cage the Ice Mage because it was cold. A discount was offered for stealing a peace treaty in Helheim. They paid without doing the job. Walker still has his. Gerk treats his as a hot rock he puts in his pants.
Plymouth confirms Walker's stone does what it is supposed to. More fire magic is theoretically possible, but without proper containment this stone would implode immediately. Walker will not try.

Keystones.existing: Magical stones used to open and connect Atlas's Arch realms.
notes: Walker is carrying his keystone along with the heat stone. Plymouth refuses to consider cramming additional magic into it. Walker jokes about modifying it and then drops the idea.
Plymouth is carrying powdered dragon liver, along with small purchases from Sunder, after forgetting most of his equipment. He has no gems.
Collapsible rod about a foot long, carried in a telescope-style pocket case on Plymouth's belt. Several turnable sections. One end is a broad, rounded, three-pronged head.

He sets it for the convergence and the 5.6-mile distance, plants it, and tells everyone to stand close. Electrical energy arcs around it, then lightning transports the group from the grassy knoll to the mountain above Langdale Stronghold. He had aimed for the front door.
It comes out smoldering and sooty. He brushes it clean and slides it back into his belt. He says a little farther off and the result would have been quite bad.

One fused item, used throughout the lantern trial. The staff half is the Staff of the Lantern Bearer. Sylan also remembers that name as the Staff of the Lantern Keeper, and the DM confirms the staff name. The lantern half is a Lantern of Revealing. A misremembered lantern name was 'lantern of the staff keeper.' Sylan, while it is active, describes the staff as having no lantern.

Play traces the lantern to Ord in Volga and the staff to Sylan at Shades and Trades. The DM says the lantern was identified at Shades and Trades. The same pieces are also listed among the magic items from the white dragon hoard, dated November 3 of the previous year. The two were already drawn together, as if polarized or magnetized, and fused in a short earlier working when the lantern's inscription was read. The DM confirms they are fused. Sylan treats that as having been part of the plan and still asks whether the inscriptions can be tried separately. He does not have the lantern on his sheet.

The lantern is hooded and finely made, with an aura of evocation and two settings. One blinded everyone in the room. Command words produced an effect the party failed to cleanly undo. On November 3, campaign year 25, Ord's experiment showed him the Ethereal Plane and blinded him until lesser restoration. No spirits were present then. The inscription is not in the DM's current notes. Ord offers 'Brightest day in darkness' as the ignition phrase. The DM treats the real wording as still to be settled.

This use is the same steps, done in the woods so bystanders would not be blinded. Ord and Sylan close their eyes. When lit, the lantern glows a desaturated blue and shows the Ethereal Plane as grayscale, semi-opaque, and ghostly, including otherwise unnoticed shadows. It is unconfirmed whether that sight penetrates magical darkness. Ethereal beings can take hold of the crook. Contact makes them burn away from the edges like paper while they howl inside the hearer's head.

When Sylan grabs the active staff, the lantern becomes incandescent shadow, a glowing roiling ball of shadow. Spirits within about four feet are vacuumed into him. He feels nothing. This is a byproduct of touching the active staff. Joined hands throw a black luminescent beacon into the sky. Letting go ends the beacon. The clearing dies in light, and a faint outline remains for a few blinks. Ord's wireframe spirit-sight continues until he turns that off separately.

Ord proposes saying the incantation backwards to shut it off. The last time they tried to turn this kind of effect off, something else happened. The backward attempt is not resolved. Sylan says they should never touch it again because it always brings those terrible things.
quotesThemes: Brightest day in darkness.
openQuestions: What is the lantern's true name, and can the staff and lantern still be separated?
What is the original inscription, and is 'Brightest day in darkness' the ignition phrase?
Can the sight see through magical darkness, and does it transfer to someone else who grips the staff?
Does speaking the incantation backwards turn the staff off, or does it cause something else?

notes: After the Grunkle took some of Ord's strength, a floating Ord solidified into a sphere or bead with a rune written on it. Dana was involved as it solidified.
Tied to the clue that the strength is hidden in Gerk and therefore cannot be restored by Dana's magic.
Looted hoard dated in the DM's notes to November 3 of the previous year.
Contained coin, about two dozen gemstones of various values, art objects of various values, mundane goods, and four or five magic items.

Pieces called out: Dana's magic broom, a set of bone dice, a shrine with a statuette, a brazier, and an altar to a god of dragon minions, a scroll with a poem, the skull of a fiend or celestial, seven candlesticks with a holy symbol, a gold birdcage later given to the crew, a box of turquoise animal figurines, Ciri's starburst ring or bracelet, and the lantern now fused to the staff.
A ring or bracelet from the white dragon hoard, believed to be in Ciri's possession. It shoots starbursts that turn into fireballs.
Heard guesses include Nightfall and Starfall. The name is not confirmed, and Ciri is absent when the party tries to remember it.
openQuestions: Is it a ring or a bracelet, and what is it called?

notes: A box of them was in the white dragon hoard. Ord inspected them and left them behind. Sylan thinks they might turn into creatures.
openQuestions: Do the turquoise animal figurines animate or transform?

notes: Dana received it from the white dragon hoard. It is the magic item she wrote down for herself from that treasure.
Its flight is 50 feet. She leaves the tower on it toward the beacon and is overtaken by Glimmen. Afterward she stomps through the group smacking people with it.
From the white dragon hoard. Sylan gave it to the crew.

Helm.existing: A helm Carlkin agreed to examine by appointment.
notes: The party also calls this worn headgear Walker's hat. Sylan wants to test whether it is the lich's phylactery, either openly or in secret. The first time Walker put it on struck Sylan as questionable. Corruption from wearing it is an open worry. Walker does not confirm or deny it.
Dana is checking her books and a Legend Lore prophetic vision to see whether this helmet could be the phylactery. That check is unresolved.

Separately, Walker wants primal stones set into his helmet for night vision, heat detection, and sight through magical darkness. He will not use his other personal jewelry for that work. He drops the idea unless the helmet can see what he wants.
openQuestions: Is this helm the lich's phylactery, and has wearing it corrupted Walker?

Ley line.existing: Lines of magic that gatehouses sit on.
notes: A convergence on these lines was identified last session. Walker has found one near his dragonrider training. Elrus did not know and is startled.
At the obelisk, the true line sits about a hundred yards off the marker. Plymouth and Elrus use that account when explaining how primal stones could be made there.
Walker learned last session what a convergence on ley lines is. Creating primal stones is easier there and takes much less effort, which is why convergences are sought after.
The one they fly toward lights up the map. Walker calls that site an obelisk. Experiencing it is meant to help his training. Plymouth calls it rare and highly magical.

Doorway.existing: A fixed supernatural passage between locations.
notes: Last session, openings could be made at different sizes and locations. The result depended on motivation, abilities, and durability, and was not cut and dry. They interact with the surroundings and with each other.
Gerk spends the day opening them from different directions while Ciri throws rocks at him, and he says the ability seems fine.

Phylactery.existing: A vessel containing a lich's soul.
notes: Dana: the phylactery must be destroyed and the lich killed before he has time to make another.
Sylan: if the party holds the soul, finding the lich should be easier. Doing the test and the destruction in the open or in secret is still undecided.
Walker's hat, also called his helmet, is the candidate under discussion. Wearing a phylactery is treated as a possible source of corruption.
openQuestions: Should the party test and destroy the phylactery in the open or in secret?

notes: Also called a beacon of eternal blackness, a beacon of blackness, and a pillar of darkness. It erupts from the treeline at the door-testing grounds when Sylan grabs the active staff, and it keeps rising while Ord and Sylan have their hands together on it.

It looks like a swirling column of ink, almost light, with a shadowy wave that can be felt passing through everything. Walker and Dana both witness it from the stronghold. Dana flies toward it, and Walker, Elrus, Araden, and Glimmen divert from the Grazog trip to follow.
When Sylan lets go, the beacon disappears. A faint outline lingers for a few blinks, and the clearing dies in light.
Sylan tries to prove himself to blinded Gerk with their call phrases and doubts Gerk will remember them.
The one Gerk has written down, and the one Sylan confirms as the first, is 'I don't trust the cat man.' Walker also offers 'scoop fruit' and 'loincloth.'
Walker's joke that Sylan is Gerk's dad is not a phrase Sylan is willing to use. Sylan says it has not been explained in a way Gerk would trust.
quotesThemes: I don't trust the cat man.

misTranscriptions.notes: DM recap of the cave conversation with Walker, and of waiting for him to leave the cave.
The other party members finished their conversation with him.
DM: the previous session ended with this person, then play starts on Walker and what he found. Unclear hearing.

Walker says Alarist thought the convergence was a good idea. The DM says primal stones are easier with Alarissa's help, in the same breath as Elrus advising the convergence, and that Walker might make a primal stone with that help. Elvis is in the same exchange: like Elvis says, the earring example would not work that way. Another hearing leaves Elvis unresolved, as the instructor agreeing with someone else present or as a misheard name.
Walker wants another gold eagle at Elrus's table in Nyx. The cave markers were generic, not this.
Gerk says he will agree, Justin, as Walker chooses the convergence.

Elrus names Gleminde and Rayodin as able to use Walker's stored gem energy to a lesser extent. One hearing says the DM then corrects toward Glimmen. Another says the DM says 'not Glimmen,' and treats Gleminde as separate from Glimmen. Later the DM asks how far Glimit can fly while timing the chase.
Paired with Gleminde as someone who could use the stored gem energy to a lesser extent. Not otherwise identified.
Sylan asks Gerk how he has been doing with the doorband thing.
Ciri ties the bee hives to the brewery's drink line while describing the tavern's mead.
Dana asks whether she is at the brewery or at this other place while trying to place herself. One hearing offers no correction; another reads it as the stronghold. Uncertain hearing.
The DM says the bee adventure was Sylan and Patty. Not an established party name.
Sylan is describing the trip where they found bees and hives.
Piano Man lyric while Dana plays: the regular crowd shuffles in.
Sylan waves as the party enters the bar where Dana is playing.
Sylan wants to talk to him about a lantern and staff, says he is going to check out Od, asks 'What's got you so down, Lord?' while talking to Ord, and later addresses Od about letting the spirit go.
Plymouth says the helmet effect needs a very powerful one.
The alternative to fire protection from an item made with the stones.
Plymouth calls Walker's proposed helmet effects quite the feats.
Plymouth says magical darkness comes from an inverse illusion or an absence of light.

Sylan and Walker's names for the landing place where they think they bought the heat stones. Plymouth later says Agenheim. Hymes echoes 'one of the Heims'; one hearing says Plymouth rejects that echo before naming Agenheim.
Sylan says they went up to Jotunheim because that is where the seeing stones were.

Plymouth's name for the unstable magical condition at the convergence, where extra magic is hard to contain: adding magic 'in a called free state like this' would be most unstable. Unclear if this is a real magical condition.
Plymouth describing forcing more magic into an item; 'can' may be capacity or a stray syllable.
Sylan: 'What was that beam?' while the table is naming the -heim lands.
Sylan: there might be a 'hidden sound' they don't know about while recalling the -heim route. Possibly a hidden town or realm.

Ord asks if the heat-stone seller will be shades and trades; Sylan and Plymouth both say no. Later Sylan says he found a staff there and fused it to the Volga lantern. The DM says Shades and Trades as the place the lantern was identified. Sylan also says Shaves and Trades. May be a shop or prior vendor name.

Sylan: 'That's where I got the field trade,' while remembering the document Nyx Cage wanted stolen, in the context of the declined peace-treaty job. May be the item or the job, not a clear known term.
Gerk: an ice maid wanted to give them a hot rock. Tongatank immediately says Nyx Cage the Ice Mage.
Plymouth's reaction while examining the heat stone.
Gerk's joke about a declaration he would have stolen.
The examining NPC is unfamiliar with the item just handed over.
The ground the obelisk sits on. The DM says 'this call island that the obelisk sits upon,' describing a rolling grassy field. Another hearing corrects it to 'small island.'
Elrus names the bright light spell: 'this is just a simple ken trip,' while producing light from a pebble and moss.
Walker: 'I'm gonna geopin this location,' marking the return coordinates. Tongatank echoes it as opening the location. Spelling of the verb is uncertain; the act is pinning the site.
Walker imagining a fancy guitar for Dana. Dana is otherwise a cleric, so this may be Walker misspeaking rather than only a transcription error.

The DM names Glimund as the one drawing the return rod from a belt during the Midgard return, then corrects himself away from Glimmen to Plymouth. Another hearing leaves the name unclear and notes the surrounding lines are Elrus planning that return. Walker says 'Thanks, Pun' immediately after Plymouth lands them on the mountain.

Ord says his strength went to a little Ord that someone else touched. The DM describes a floating form after the Grunkle fight that solidified into a runic bead or rune-marked sphere. One hearing corrects the heard 'Ord' to 'orb.'
Sylan, preparing the lantern work, checks that he has it so the test does not blind them. The context is not blinding themselves. No correction given.
Walker: 'this whole fucking l cosmic loom thing.'
Ord's attempt to name where his strength was lost: 'We were at the orc. Tam.' The DM later identifies the fight with Gerk's uncle.
Secrets operative the party could not name: our man, our secrets. Ord corrects from the rat to the rack guy. The DM told them to remember where they left him. Sylan treats him as away without leave.
DM's word for the origin of Ord's strength loss when offering a refresher.

The DM's name for the little gold roommate. Ord says Ponchi is his roommate. Archie is Ord's first correction while the roommate is being identified, immediately followed by Ponchi. One hearing records Archie with no correction.
Shrine piece in the white dragon hoard, with a statuette and an altar.
Dana confirming the loot was the white dragon's hoard.

Sylan's wording for the fused item. One hearing says the DM agrees. Another says the DM only agreed it was in the right direction, then the table slid into the reversed joke name, and the real name was still unknown.

Ord's reversed joke name for the lantern paired with the Staff of the Lantern Keeper. Sylan rejects it as not the weird real name. The DM echoes the start of the phrase ('lantern of the staff keep'). Real name still unknown.
Ord's first wording for the lantern aura. He corrects himself to evocation a moment later.
Ord describing the check that found the lantern's aura.
Sylan asks Aris whether it was shared into his journal while they search notes for the identified item.

Said right after the hoard totals, about the dragon whose name they cannot remember. One hearing corrects it to the phrase 'lost to time.' Another treats it as Sylan's first guess at the undead hoard-owner's name, immediately replaced by Lady Meriwether, and is unsure it was a real candidate.

newTerms.name: Primal stone
notes: A gem in which elemental energy, such as Walker's fire, is stabilized so it can be set into a weapon or other conduit. A weapon set with one deals that energy's damage and magic damage.
Capacity depends on energy spent and gem purity, and making one costs more energy than it stores. It is much easier at a ley-line convergence. Walker may be able to make one with Elrus's help.
Walker's raw gems are not primal stones yet. Only dragon-linked people can safely handle that raw store; others need the finished stone set into an object.

Once set with a cosmic loom, the number, value, and setting decide the effect: offensive fire, fire protection, warmth, light, heat detection, piercing magical darkness, or night vision. Walker is waiting so the party can choose.

newTerms.name: Ley-line convergence
notes: A rare, highly magical place where ley lines meet. Primal stones take much less effort there, and Plymouth says experiencing this one will aid Walker's training.
The site Walker and Plymouth are flying to lights up the map. Walker calls that mark an obelisk, but the standing stone is shifted about a hundred yards off the true convergence.
Elrus had not been told of the one Walker found and treats it as important.

newTerms.name: Obelisk

Walker uses the name for the convergence marked on the map. The stone itself sits off the true ley-line point.

newTerms.name: Cosmic loom
notes: A magical containment table, also known by other names: an altar-like upside-down table whose four corner pillars form a containing field. It is required to set a primal stone into an object.
Elrus does not know where one is, and Walker had not heard of one. Plymouth says the party cannot make one, at least not quickly.
Walker held off imbuing a stone until the party decides, and does not yet see how a primal stone solves the lack of a loom.

The inscription is known to Ord but was not written down. Lit, the lantern draws spirits that burn away on contact.
